rulings.challenge_claim: Row's back boundary at 6:23 mischaracterizes 6:24 as opening independent material naming a fresh threat not yet in view; the infinitive-of-purpose clause at 6:24 grammatically completes the sentence begun at 6:23 (WEB joins them with a comma, not a period), and no petuchah corroborates a seam there.
rulings.grounds: WEB byte tier (verse_map_web.json) confirms Prov.6.23 ends “...are the way of life,” (comma) continuing directly into Prov.6.24 “to keep you from the immoral woman...” as one sentence. oshb byte tier confirms Prov.6.24 opens with the bare infinitive construct לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ (no coordinating waw, no new subject), attaching as a purpose clause to the preceding motive clause of 6:23 (כִּ֤י ... , "for"), not introducing independent material. pmarks_Prov.json marks confirm zero PE/SAMEKH between Prov.6.19 (before this row) and Prov.6.26 (inside the FOLLOWING row P03-010) -- the claimed 6:23/6:24 seam carries no parashah corroboration either way. Precision correction: LF's own citation that the construction recurs verse-for-verse at oshb:Prov.7.5 overstates the match -- independently re-ran sweep.py --skel on the opener (skeleton tier; 2 book-wide verse hits: Prov.6.24, Prov.7.5) -- only the OPENING WORD לִ֭שְׁמָרְךָ is shared; the governed noun phrase differs (מֵאֵ֣שֶׁת רָ֑ע מֵֽ֝חֶלְקַ֗ת לָשׁ֥וֹן נָכְרִיָּֽה at 6:24 vs מֵאִשָּׁ֣ה זָרָ֑ה מִ֝נָּכְרִיָּ֗ה אֲמָרֶ֥יהָ הֶחֱלִֽיקָה at 7:5). This does not affect the core finding.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite the rejected_alternative so it no longer states 6:24 opens material naming a fresh addressee-threat not yet in view; disclose instead that the infinitive-of-purpose at 6:24 is the grammatical continuation of 6:23's motive clause. Because the 6:23/6:24 seam has neither vocative-restart nor parashah corroboration (nearest PE marks sit at 6:19, before the unit, and 6:26, inside the next row), re-derive the boundary against the owner's C1 corroboration pattern; the byte-grounded candidate is a merged instruction_lecture bounded at the corroborated petuchah of Prov.6.26 (or through the 6:29 application clause, if a longer unit is preferred). This is a boundary-change PROPOSAL only and requires explicit boss adoption. Test the cure must pass: the revised row must not characterize a purpose-infinitive clause lacking a coordinating conjunction as opening independent material, and its chosen edge(s) must each carry a named vocative-restart or parashah corroboration, or an explicit disclosed rationale for why neither applies.

rulings.challenge_claim: Rationale frames 6:24's purpose infinitive as governing the whole span from a fresh start, but the same clause is the grammatical tail of the sentence opened at 6:23, so the front boundary overstates 6:24's independence.
rulings.grounds: Confirmed by the same byte evidence as the P03-009/LF ruling above (WEB comma-continuity 6:23-6:24; oshb 6:24 bare infinitive with no coordinator; pmarks_Prov.json shows no PE/SAMEKH at the 6:23/6:24 seam). Correction to the challenge's framing: P03-010's own rationale text does not literally use the phrase fresh start -- that wording is the SIBLING row P03-009's rejected_alternative, not P03-010's own field. The defect in P03-010 itself is narrower but still real: it describes 6:24's infinitive as what governs the whole span without disclosing that the same clause depends grammatically on the preceding row's 6:23 clause. This is the same underlying seam-level defect as the P03-009/LF item, not a distinct one -- both challenge items describe one seam from its two sides.
rulings.remedy: Same cure as the P03-009/LF item (seam-pair cure, one edit covering both rows): add explicit disclosure in P03-010's rationale that its own governing infinitive is the syntactic continuation of 6:23, and apply the same boundary re-derivation against the owner's C1 corroboration pattern before finalizing whether 6:24 remains a row-initial verse. Boundary change is a PROPOSAL only, requires boss adoption.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two WEB citations break the mandatory curly-quote-with-inline-ref convention by rendering verbatim WEB text in straight quotes, and one of those (will not spare in the day of vengeance) does not match the cited witness's actual wording.
rulings.grounds: Byte tier (verse_map_web.json) confirms web:Prov.6.34 reads “For jealousy arouses the fury of the husband. He won’t spare in the day of vengeance.” -- the row's quoted string will not spare in the day of vengeance omits He and substitutes will not for the source's contraction won't, so it is not a verbatim substring. Independently re-ran check_web_quotes.py over all 8 rows in the cluster (20 curly-quoted spans checked, 0 flags, GREEN) -- confirming the tool scans only CURLY-quoted spans and is structurally blind to straight-quote convention breaches, so this defect could not be machine-caught and required the manual/model catch LF performed. A cluster-wide scan for straight-quoted 3+ word English spans found no other instance of this defect in the remaining 7 rows -- the issue is isolated to P03-011.
rulings.remedy: Re-cut both straight-quoted spans to curly quotes with byte-verbatim WEB text: “is void of understanding” (verbatim substring already, only the quote marks need fixing) and the vengeance clause corrected to a verbatim substring of web:Prov.6.34, e.g. “won't spare in the day of vengeance” (dropping the non-verbatim will not, or including He if the fuller clause is wanted). Test the cure must pass: check_web_quotes.py GREEN plus a manual straight-quote scan of the revised row returning no 3+ word English spans in straight quotes paired with a web: ref.

rulings.challenge_claim: The span (6:20-23) omits disclosure of the paseq mark at 6:22, a span-relevant mark the campaign's mark-disclosure symmetry rule requires unconditionally.
rulings.grounds: pmarks_Prov.json paseq inventory carries Prov.6.22: 1; independently re-derived that this ref falls inside the row's own Prov.6.20-Prov.6.23 span. Ran a full disclosure-symmetry sweep (script cross-checking every marks/paseq/kq ref against every row's own span) over all 8 rows in the cluster: only two undisclosed-mark gaps exist in the entire cluster -- this one and the P04-003/OL gaps below; no other row in c05 has an undisclosed span-relevant mark. CONVERGENCE: this is a DISTINCT defect from the LF challenge on the same row (P03-009/LF above) -- LF's challenge concerns the back-boundary's grammatical characterization, this one concerns mark-disclosure symmetry; both hold independently and do not overlap.
rulings.remedy: Add a disclosure entry (device_notes or observed_substrate_signals) naming the paseq at Prov.6.22 as tier-3, single-witness, count-only (not positional), matching the disclosure pattern already used correctly elsewhere in the cluster (P04-001's paseq at 7:12; P04-004's paseq at 8:29/8:30). Test: check_marks.py span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry check must pass on the revised row.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row reads the purpose-infinitive opener at 7:5 as unit-internal continuity, but the identical opener recurs at only one other place, 6:24, which this cluster's own earlier rows treat as what starts a fresh unit, and the row's rejected_alternative never tests the analogous split at 7:4/7:5.
rulings.grounds: Independently re-ran sweep.py --skel on the opener (skeleton tier): confirms exactly 2 book-wide verse hits, Prov.6.24 and Prov.7.5 -- the sweep-digit premise is accurate. The normative inference runs the wrong direction, however: oshb byte tier confirms BOTH occurrences are bare infinitives-of-purpose with NO coordinating conjunction, which in Hebrew syntax attach BACKWARD to the preceding clause/imperative chain -- they do not open independent material. Per the adjudication of the P03-009/LF and P03-010/LF items above, the premise that this cluster's own two rows earlier treat 6:24 as what starts a fresh unit describes P03-009/P03-010's DEFECTIVE framing (corrected above via uphold/refine rulings), not an established correct precedent -- so it cannot be used to fault P04-001 for not mirroring it. P04-001's own treatment of 7:5 (purpose clause continuing the 7:1-4 imperative chain, picked up by the causal opener of oshb:Prov.7.6) is grammatically the CORRECT reading, symmetric with the corrected understanding of 6:24, not inconsistent with it.

rulings.challenge_claim: The span (8:1-21) omits disclosure of three span-relevant marks (paseq at 8:13, paseq at 8:21, and a ketiv/qere note at 8:17), and at both of its internal candidate seams states parashah silence itself as the ground for merging rather than splitting -- the inverse of the standing rule that parashah absence is never a boundary argument in either direction.
rulings.grounds: pmarks_Prov.json confirms paseq at Prov.8.13:1 and Prov.8.21:1, and kq at Prov.8.17:1, all falling inside the row's Prov.8.1-Prov.8.21 span; independently re-derived via a full disclosure-symmetry sweep of all 8 rows -- only this row and P03-009/OL have any gap in the whole cluster. Directly inspected oshb byte tier for Prov.8.17: "אֲ֭נִי אהביה אֹהֲבַ֣י אֵהָ֑ב וּ֝מְשַׁחֲרַ֗י יִמְצָאֻֽנְנִי" -- confirms the unpointed ketiv אהביה (3fs, who love her) sits inline directly before the pointed qere אֹהֲבַ֣י (1cs, who love me) inside the first-person self-commendation the row argues runs unbroken from 8:12-21, exactly the inline-ketiv hazard class TOOLKIT.md flags for disclosure. The petuchah at 8:21 IS disclosed in the row but the co-located paseq at that same verse is never named -- confirmed by direct field inspection, distinct from the petuchah disclosure. Also confirmed byte-true by direct field inspection: the row's own rationale/rejected_alternative state, verbatim, that nothing in the parashah layer marks a seam at 8:3/8:4, and that nothing in the parashah layer marks a seam at 8:11/8:12, in both cases as the STATED GROUND for keeping the material merged -- directly contradicting the standing rule (TOOLKIT.md; pmarks_Prov.json marks_note) that parashah absence is NEVER counterevidence and never a boundary driver in either direction.
rulings.remedy: (a) Add disclosure entries for the paseq at Prov.8.13 and Prov.8.21 (alongside the existing 8:21 petuchah disclosure) and for the K/Q at Prov.8.17, naming it as a live inline-ketiv site bearing on grammatical person/voice within the self-commendation the row argues is unified. (b) Rewrite both internal-seam arguments (8:3/8:4 and 8:11/8:12) to rest only on the affirmative byte evidence already available in the row -- the third-to-first-person shift at אֲלֵיכֶ֣ם (oshb:Prov.8.4) and the self-declaration formula אֲֽנִי חָ֭כְמָה opening oshb:Prov.8.12 -- and remove both parashah-silence-as-ground statements entirely, since absence must never be argued from in either direction. Test the cure must pass: check_marks.py mark-disclosure symmetry must pass, and a text scan of the revised rationale/rejected_alternative must contain no parashah-absence phrasing offered as a merge (or split) warrant.
